## 1. Executive Summary

To determine the time-dependent solar wind proton and heavy-ion conditions incident on interstellar comet **3I/ATLAS (`C/2025 N1`)** at heliocentric distance $r = 1.870\text{--}1.882\text{ AU}$ ($\text{HCI latitude} = -6.46^\circ$) during its **3–4 December 2025 XMM-Newton EPIC observation (`ObsID 0963720201`)**, we designed, implemented, verified, and validated a GPU-accelerated **3D spherical ideal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) simulation code** (`src/heliomhd3d.cu`) covering the inner heliosphere from $r_{\rm in} = 0.10\text{ AU}$ ($21.5\,R_\odot$) to $r_{\rm out} = 2.40\text{ AU}$.

Our investigation resolves the discrepancy between the preprint's empirical 1D ballistic Parker extrapolation (`analysis_repro/analysis_06_solar_wind`, which estimated $\Phi_{\rm SW} \approx (2\text{--}6)\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$ around a reference of $6\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$ and required a low solar wind heavy-ion fraction $f_{\rm hi} \approx 2.9\times 10^{-4}$ to explain the observed XMM-Newton EPIC-pn X-ray count rate) and the external reviewer's recommended **NASA CCMC WSA 5.4 + ENLIL 2.8f** simulation (`Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1`, which predicted $\Phi_{p,\text{helio}} = 4.51\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$ and $\Phi_{p,\text{comet}} = 4.07\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$ during the observation):

1. **Multi-Spacecraft 1 AU Validation Reveals a $2\times$ Mass-Flux Deficit in Uncalibrated CCMC ENLIL**:
   Direct comparison against native 1 AU in-situ plasma measurements (`STEREO-A` PLASTIC, `Wind` SWE, `ACE` SWEPAM, and `Solar Orbiter` SWA-PAS) over `2025-11-26` to `2025-12-05` demonstrates that the default uncalibrated CCMC ENLIL inner boundary (`dfast = 125 cm^-3` at $21.5\,R_\odot$, corresponding to $\sim 2.75\text{ cm}^{-3}$ fast-wind density at $1\text{ AU}$) systematically **underpredicts observed 1 AU solar wind proton flux by a factor of $\sim 2\times$** (median model-to-observed flux ratio `Uncal/Obs = 0.50` at `STEREO-A` and `0.56` at `Wind`). Furthermore, the static magnetogram boundary misses the sharp phase and amplitude of the high-speed stream and Corotating Interaction Region (CIR) observed in situ by `STEREO-A` on `2025-11-28/29` ($n_p$ peaking at $34\text{ cm}^{-3}$, $|\mathbf{v}_{\rm SW}|$ rising from $375$ to $710\text{ km s}^{-1}$).
2. **Three-Tier Inner Boundary Hierarchy Quantifies Input Epistemic Uncertainty**:
   Because inner-boundary specification dominates the uncertainty at $1.87\text{ AU}$, we drive our 3D spherical ideal-MHD solver with three self-consistent inner boundary models at $r_{\rm in} = 0.10\text{ AU}$:
   - **Model 1 (`model1_ccmc`, Uncalibrated WSA 5.4 / CCMC-Scale)**: Reproduces CCMC ENLIL v2.8f at 3I/ATLAS (`PN-GTI mean` $n_p = 0.87\text{ cm}^{-3}$, $|\mathbf{v}_{\rm SW}| = 480.5\text{ km s}^{-1}$, comet-frame relative speed $v_{\rm rel} = 443.2\text{ km s}^{-1}$, heliocentric flux $\Phi_{p,\text{helio}} = 4.16\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$, comet-frame incident flux $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 3.83\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$).
   - **Model 2 (`model2_wsa_cal`, 1 AU Momentum-Flux Calibrated WSA 5.4)**: Scales the 25 dynamic GONGZ WSA 5.4 maps to match observed 1 AU momentum flux (`PN-GTI mean` $n_p = 1.95\text{ cm}^{-3}$, $|\mathbf{v}_{\rm SW}| = 452.1\text{ km s}^{-1}$, $v_{\rm rel} = 414.1\text{ km s}^{-1}$, $\Phi_{p,\text{helio}} = 8.83\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$, $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 8.09\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$).
   - **Model 3 (`model3_assimilated`, Multi-Spacecraft Data-Assimilated + WSA 2D Latitudinal Structure)**: Assimilates the corotating `STEREO-A` (`lat = -5.36 deg`, closest in latitude to 3I/ATLAS at `-6.46 deg`), `Wind`/`ACE` (`lat = +0.51 deg`), and `Solar Orbiter` (`lat = +9.44 deg`) streams onto the $0.10\text{ AU}$ inner boundary while preserving WSA 5.4 latitudinal gradients. It achieves a 1 AU median flux ratio of `Mod3/Obs = 1.04` at `STEREO-A` and `1.03` at `Wind`. An out-of-sample holdout run (`model3_holdout_wind`, trained strictly on `STEREO-A` + `Solar Orbiter` with `Wind` and `ACE` completely withheld) predicts the out-of-sample `Wind` L1 solar wind with speed $\text{RMSE} = 67.3\text{ km s}^{-1}$ ($r = 0.728$) and median flux ratio `1.032`.
3. **3D MHD Stream Evolution & Timing at 3I/ATLAS**:
   In both **Model 3 (Assimilated 3D MHD)** and the **Out-of-Sample Holdout**, the fast corotating stream and CIR observed by `STEREO-A` on Nov 28–29 steepens into a forward-reverse compression wave between $1.0\text{ AU}$ and $1.87\text{ AU}$. Because magnetosonic fast-mode pressure waves and shock fronts propagate faster than the slow ahead plasma while the stream interface itself is decelerated by momentum exchange with the slow wind ahead, **the trailing half of the compressed CIR density pileup sweeps across 3I/ATLAS during the first half of the XMM-Newton observation (`2025-12-03 12:04 UTC` to `2025-12-04 04:00 UTC`)**, transitioning into the high-speed rarefaction stream ($|\mathbf{v}_{\rm SW}| \approx 645\text{ km s}^{-1}$, $n_p \approx 0.8\text{ cm}^{-3}$, $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} \approx 5.2\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$) by the end of the EPIC-pn exposure (`2025-12-04 10:12 UTC`).
   - Over the **45 accepted EPIC-pn science GTIs (`21.36 ks`)**, our fine-grid ($224\times 48\times 240$, $1.5^\circ$) Model 3 simulation gives a **GTI-mean comet-frame incident proton flux of $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 2.104\times 10^8\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$** (heliocentric flux $\Phi_{p,\text{helio}} = 2.278\times 10^8\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$).
   - Over the continuous **EPIC-pn frame-header window (`Dec 3 12:04` – `Dec 4 10:12 UTC`)**, the window mean is $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 1.713\times 10^8\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$ and the **window median is $1.459\times 10^8\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$**.
   - Over the **all-pointing XMM window (`Dec 3 12:38` – `Dec 4 17:22 UTC`)**, the window mean is $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 1.376\times 10^8\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$ and the **window median is $9.425\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$**.
4. **Rigorous Numerical Convergence & Physical Controls**:
   - **Spatial Grid Convergence**: Across four 3D grids ($80\times 16\times 90$ [$4^\circ$], $120\times 24\times 120$ [$3^\circ$], $160\times 32\times 180$ [$2^\circ$], and $224\times 48\times 240$ [$1.5^\circ$]), the EPIC-pn GTI mean incident proton flux converges to within **`-0.60%`** (Medium vs. Fine) and **`+2.14%`** (Baseline vs. Fine).
   - **Temporal Step Size (CFL)**: Halving the Courant number (`CFL = 0.175` vs. `0.35`, doubling the number of RK2 steps from $6{,}353$ to $12{,}705$) changes the GTI mean incident flux by only **`+0.30%`**.
   - **Latitudinal Domain Extent**: Varying the polar domain from $\pm 30^\circ$ to $\pm 45^\circ$ and $\pm 60^\circ$ changes the GTI mean incident flux by **`-1.02%`** and **`+2.77%`**.
   - **16 DONKI Cone CMEs**: Injecting all 16 DONKI cone CMEs (including the two Nov 23 filament-eruption CMEs aimed toward 3I/ATLAS's quadrant at central launch speeds of $397$ and $425\text{ km s}^{-1}$) changes the EPIC-pn GTI mean incident flux by **`< 0.01%`** because those Nov 23 CMEs sweep past $1.87\text{ AU}$ on Nov 30–Dec 1 (3 days prior to the XMM observation), unless extreme drag deceleration were invoked.
   - **Why Full 3D MHD ($\mathbf{B}\ne 0$) Is Essential**: A pure hydrodynamic control run ($\mathbf{B}=0$, `phys_hydro_only`) lacking magnetic pressure and tension over-compresses the CIR shock interface at $1.87\text{ AU}$ by **`+74.8%`** relative to full 3D MHD! Including the interplanetary magnetic field ($|B| \approx 1.7\text{ nT}$ in the CIR at $1.87\text{ AU}$) provides fast-magnetosonic wave dispersion that prevents unphysical hydrodynamic shock over-steepening.

## 3. Coordinate Systems, Ephemeris Verification, and Comet Kinematics

All spatial coordinates in our 3D MHD simulation are defined in the **Heliocentric Inertial (HCI)** frame (`r` in AU, colatitude $\theta = 90^\circ - \text{lat}_{\rm HCI}$, longitude $\phi = \text{lon}_{\rm HCI} \in [0, 360^\circ)$) defined by the IAU 1986/2015 Solar North Pole ($\alpha_0 = 286.13^\circ$, $\delta_0 = 63.87^\circ$ in J2000 equatorial coordinates) and the ascending node of the solar equator on the J2000 ecliptic (`scripts/prepare_inputs.py`):
$$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{z,\text{HCI}} = (-0.000000,\; 0.126196,\; 0.992005)_{\text{Ecl,J2000}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{x,\text{HCI}} = (-0.126196,\; 0.992005 \times 0,\; \dots) \implies \Omega_{\rm node} = 75.76^\circ.$$
We verified our coordinate transformation (`scripts/prepare_inputs.py`, `data/processed/ephemeris_summary.json`) against the NASA CCMC ENLIL trajectory headers (`Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1_evo_3I-Atlas1_20251001T00.dat`, `earth1`, `stereoa1`, `solo1`), achieving **$< 0.01^\circ$ angular agreement and $< 10^{-4}\text{ AU}$ radial agreement** across all four targets at the observation midpoint (`MJD 61012.9639`, `2025-12-03 23:08 UTC`):
- **3I/ATLAS (`C/2025 N1`)**: $r = 1.8732\text{ AU}$, $\text{lat}_{\rm HCI} = -6.46^\circ$, $\text{lon}_{\rm HCI} = 135.42^\circ$ ($\text{HEEQ lon} = +152.95^\circ$ ahead of Earth). Velocity in local spherical RTN coordinates: $v_R = +43.13\text{ km s}^{-1}$ (outbound), $v_T = -49.43\text{ km s}^{-1}$ (retrograde), $v_N = +2.17\text{ km s}^{-1}$ ($|\mathbf{v}_{3\mathrm{I}}| = 65.64\text{ km s}^{-1}$).

## 4. 3D Spherical Ideal-MHD Numerical Formulation (`src/heliomhd3d.cu`)

### 4.1 Governing Conservation Laws & Source Terms
We solve the 3D compressible ideal-MHD equations with solar gravity, Dedner hyperbolic-parabolic divergence cleaning, and passive heavy-ion composition advection in spherical coordinates $(r, \theta, \phi)$ (`src/heliomhd3d.cu`):
$$\frac{\partial \mathbf{U}}{\partial t} + \frac{1}{r^2}\frac{\partial}{\partial r}\!\left(r^2 \mathbf{F}_r\right) + \frac{1}{r\sin\theta}\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}\!\left(\sin\theta\,\mathbf{F}_\theta\right) + \frac{1}{r\sin\theta}\frac{\partial \mathbf{F}_\phi}{\partial \phi} = \mathbf{S}_{\rm geom}(\mathbf{U}) + \mathbf{S}_{\rm grav}(\mathbf{U}) + \mathbf{S}_{\rm Dedner}(\mathbf{U}),$$
where the 10-component state vector is $\mathbf{U} = (\rho,\, \rho v_r,\, \rho v_\theta,\, \rho v_\phi,\, E,\, B_r,\, B_\theta,\, B_\phi,\, \psi,\, \rho f_{\rm hi})^{\mathsf{T}}$, total energy density is $E = \frac{p}{\gamma - 1} + \frac{1}{2}\rho |\mathbf{v}|^2 + \frac{1}{2}|\mathbf{B}|^2$, and total pressure is $p_{\rm tot} = p + \frac{1}{2}|\mathbf{B}|^2$.
- **Exact Spherical Finite-Volume Geometry**: Cell volumes $\Delta V_{i,j} = \frac{1}{3}(r_{i+1/2}^3 - r_{i-1/2}^3)(\cos\theta_{j-1/2} - \cos\theta_{j+1/2})\Delta\phi$ and face areas are computed analytically so that uniform states and $r^{-2}$ radial fluxes are preserved to machine precision.
- **Spherical Geometric & Gravitational Curvature Terms**: Include hydrodynamic and Maxwell stress curvature terms in the $r$, $\theta$, and $\phi$ momentum equations plus solar gravity $S_{{\rm grav},\,r} = -\rho GM_\odot/r^2$ and $S_{{\rm grav},\,E} = -\rho v_r GM_\odot/r^2$.
- **Polytropic Index**: Baseline runs use $\gamma = 1.50$ (matching standard inner-heliosphere ENLIL polytropic heating that reproduces observed radial temperature profiles $T(r) \propto r^{-1}$), with a dedicated $\gamma = 5/3$ adiabatic sensitivity control (`phys_gamma_53`).
- **Reconstruction, Riemann Solver & Time Integration**: 2nd-order piecewise-linear TVD reconstruction on primitive variables $(\rho, \mathbf{v}, p, \mathbf{B}, \psi, f_{\rm hi})$ with generalized minmod limiter ($\theta_{\rm lim} = 1.5$), local Lax-Friedrichs (Rusanov/HLL) approximate Riemann solver using the exact fast magnetosonic wave speed $c_f = \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}[c_s^2 + v_A^2 + \sqrt{(c_s^2+v_A^2)^2 - 4c_s^2 v_{A,n}^2}]}$, Dedner et al. (2002) $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{B}$ cleaning ($c_h = 0.8\,\Delta h/\Delta t$, $\tau_p = \Delta h/(0.18\,c_h)$), and 2nd-order strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta (SSP-RK2) time integration.
- **Passive Heavy-Ion Scalar $f_{\rm hi}$**: Advected conservatively via $\partial_t(\rho f_{\rm hi}) + \nabla\cdot(\rho f_{\rm hi}\mathbf{v}) = 0$, initialized on the inner boundary using the empirical Schwadron & Cravens (2000) / Bodewits et al. (2007) slow/fast wind oxygen-equivalent SWCX composition scaling ($f_{\rm hi} \approx 7.5\times 10^{-4}$ in slow streamer wind $v \lesssim 400\text{ km s}^{-1}$, transitioning smoothly to $f_{\rm hi} \approx 3.8\times 10^{-4}$ in fast coronal-hole wind $v \gtrsim 650\text{ km s}^{-1}$).

1. **1D Brio & Wu (1988) Coplanar MHD Shock Tube (`--mode brio_wu`, Panels a–b)**:
   - Run on grids of $N = 400$, $800$, and $1600$ cells to $t = 0.10$ with $\gamma = 2.0$ and $B_x = 0.75$.
   - Accurately captures all five MHD wave structures: left-going fast rarefaction (`FR`), compound slow magnetosonic wave (`SM`), contact discontinuity (`CD`, across which the passive heavy-ion scalar $f_{\rm hi}$ jumps sharply without oscillation), right-going slow shock (`SS`), and right-going fast rarefaction (`FR`).
   - Measured $L_1$ density errors relative to the $N=1600$ reference are $L_1(400) = 4.308\times 10^{-3}$ and $L_1(800) = 1.638\times 10^{-3}$, giving a **convergence ratio of $2.630$** (convergence order $1.395$, optimal for shock-capturing TVD schemes on discontinuous solutions).
2. **3D Spherical Axisymmetric Parker / Weber-Davis Steady Magnetized Wind (`--mode parker`, Panels c–d)**:
   - Run on three 3D spherical grids ($48\times 12\times 48$, $96\times 24\times 96$, and $192\times 48\times 192$) from $r = 0.10\text{ AU}$ to $2.40\text{ AU}$ and compared against exact 1D fourth-order Runge-Kutta integration of the steady spherical MHD ODE (`compute_exact_parker_ode`).

3. **3D Tilted-Dipole ($30^\circ$) Corotating Interaction Region (CIR) Benchmark (`--mode cir`, Panels e–f)**:
   - Simulates a $30^\circ$ tilted magnetic dipole streamer belt ($v_{\rm slow} = 330\text{ km s}^{-1}$, $n_{\rm slow} = 1100\text{ cm}^{-3}$ at $0.10\text{ AU}$) embedded in fast coronal-hole wind ($v_{\rm fast} = 680\text{ km s}^{-1}$, $n_{\rm fast} = 260\text{ cm}^{-3}$) across three 3D grids ($64\times 16\times 64$, $128\times 32\times 128$, and $192\times 48\times 192$).
   - Reproduces the classic Pizzo (1982, 1991) and Gosling & Pizzo (1999) 3D CIR evolution: smooth sinusoidal longitudinal variations at $0.10\text{ AU}$ steepen into a sawtooth velocity profile at $1.00\text{ AU}$ and form a forward-reverse magnetosonic shock pair bounding a compressed density pileup ($n_p \approx 10.2\text{ cm}^{-3}$) and magnetic field compression ($|B| \approx 6.2\text{ nT}$) at $r = 1.873\text{ AU}$, with clear monotonic convergence from $64^3$ to $128^3$ and $192^3$.

Because $T(r)$ cools with heliocentric distance, the hydrodynamic Mach number of the stream interface is much higher than the fast magnetosonic Mach number, causing the CIR pileup to over-steepen by **`+74.8%`** ($n_p$ peaking at $>11\text{ cm}^{-3}$ during the GTI window). Including full 3D MHD ($\mathbf{B} \ne 0$) provides magnetic pressure support within the stream interface that broadens and moderates the compression wave.
2. **Role of Solar Gravity ($GM_\odot$)**: Turning off solar gravity (`phys_no_grav`) eliminates the $\sim 18\text{--}25\text{ km s}^{-1}$ gravitational deceleration between $0.10\text{ AU}$ and $1.87\text{ AU}$, causing the CIR compression peak to arrive $\sim 8\text{ hours}$ earlier on Dec 3 and shifting the observation window further into the trailing rarefaction (`-34.5%` GTI mean flux).
3. **Role of Polytropic Index ($\gamma = 5/3$ vs. $1.5$)**: Increasing $\gamma$ from $1.5$ to $5/3$ (`phys_gamma_53`) increases thermal pressure acceleration inside $0.3\text{ AU}$ (`+9.6 km/s` faster wind at $1.87\text{ AU}$) and cools the outer heliosphere more rapidly ($T \propto r^{-4/3}$ vs. $r^{-1}$), sharpening the CIR compression by `+12.1%`.
4. **Role of the 16 DONKI Cone CMEs (Including the Nov 23 Filament-Eruption CMEs)**: As noted in collaborator audits (`claude_20261016T2345Z_inputs_cme_sir.md` and `codex_external_model_20261016T2334Z_nov23_cme_correction.txt`), the CCMC run omitted two Nov 23 DONKI CMEs (`2025-11-23T06:36Z` at $397\text{ km s}^{-1}$ and `2025-11-23T19:13Z` at $425\text{ km s}^{-1}$) launched toward 3I/ATLAS's quadrant ($\text{HEEQ lon} \approx 141^\circ\text{--}168^\circ$). Our `phys_with_cmes` run injects all **16 DONKI cone CMEs** (including both Nov 23 CMEs in `data/processed/cmes_hci.txt` at their measured $21.5\,R_\odot$ passages and speeds). Because they propagate at $\sim 410\text{--}460\text{ km s}^{-1}$ embedded in the ambient wind, their disturbances sweep past $1.873\text{ AU}$ on **Nov 30–Dec 1** ($\sim 3\text{ days}$ before the XMM observation), leaving the Dec 3–4 EPIC-pn window unchanged to within **`< 0.01%`**. Only if an extreme drag scenario decelerated those Nov 23 transients to $< 305\text{ km s}^{-1}$ mean transit speed could their trailing flanks overlap early Dec 3; even then, the corotating `STEREO-A` CIR arrival already dominates the Dec 3–4 density enhancement.

## 1. Summary of Completed Deliverables

## 2. Final Quantitative Results at 3I/ATLAS (`ObsID 0963720201`)
We report both **heliocentric** and **comet-frame relative** ($|\mathbf{v}_{\rm SW} - \mathbf{v}_{3\mathrm{I}}|$, which is $7.5\%\text{--}9.5\%$ lower due to 3I/ATLAS's $+43.13\text{ km s}^{-1}$ outbound radial velocity) speeds and fluxes across all three XMM-Newton window definitions:
1. **Model 1 (`model1_ccmc`, Uncalibrated WSA 5.4 / CCMC-Scale `dfast=125`)**:
   - **Accepted EPIC-pn GTIs (`21.36 ks`)**: $n_p = 0.87\text{ cm}^{-3}$, $|\mathbf{v}_{\rm SW}| = 480.5\text{ km s}^{-1}$ ($v_{\rm rel} = 443.2\text{ km s}^{-1}$), heliocentric proton flux $\Phi_{p,\text{helio}} = 4.16\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$, **comet-frame incident flux $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 3.83\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$** ($\Phi_{\rm hi,rel} = 2.46\times 10^4\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$).
   - Matches NASA CCMC WSA 5.4 + ENLIL 2.8f (`Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1`: $n_p = 1.11\text{ cm}^{-3}$, $|\mathbf{v}_{\rm SW}| = 408.0\text{ km s}^{-1}$, $\Phi_{p,\text{helio}} = 4.51\times 10^7$, $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 4.07\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$), which we showed underpredicts 1 AU spacecraft proton flux by $\sim 2\times$ (`Mod1/Obs = 0.50` at `STEREO-A`, `0.56` at `Wind`).
2. **Model 2 (`model2_wsa_cal`, 1 AU Momentum-Flux Calibrated WSA 5.4)**:
   - **Accepted EPIC-pn GTIs (`21.36 ks`)**: $n_p = 1.95\text{ cm}^{-3}$, $|\mathbf{v}_{\rm SW}| = 452.1\text{ km s}^{-1}$ ($v_{\rm rel} = 414.1\text{ km s}^{-1}$), $\Phi_{p,\text{helio}} = 8.83\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$, **comet-frame incident flux $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 8.09\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$** ($\Phi_{\rm hi,rel} = 5.66\times 10^4\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$).
   - **PN Frame Window (`Dec 3 12:04–Dec 4 10:12 UTC`)**: Mean $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 8.51\times 10^7$, median $8.62\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$.
   - Resolves the apparent $1.5\times\text{--}2\times$ offset between CCMC ENLIL and the preprint's ballistic `STEREO-A`/`Wind`/`ACE` extrapolations (`6.95e7–7.51e7 cm^-2 s^-1` median).
3. **Model 3 (`model3_assimilated` & `res_fine_224x48x240`, Multi-Spacecraft Data-Assimilated 3D MHD)**:
   - Captures the exact phase and amplitude of the Nov 28–29 `STEREO-A` CIR (`Mod3/Obs = 1.04` at `STEREO-A`, `1.03` at `Wind`, and out-of-sample `Wind` holdout `1.032` with speed $r = 0.728$).
   - Predicts that the trailing slope of the compressed CIR stream interface sweeps across 3I/ATLAS during `2025-12-03 12:04` – `2025-12-04 04:00 UTC` (coinciding with the initial $4.28\text{ ct s}^{-1}$ peak in the EPIC-pn X-ray lightcurve) before relaxing into the fast coronal-hole stream ($\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} \approx 5.2\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$ by `Dec 4 10:12 UTC`).
   - **Fine Grid (`224x48x240`, $1.5^\circ$) Summary**:
     - **Accepted EPIC-pn GTIs (`21.36 ks`)**: Mean $n_p = 4.06\text{ cm}^{-3}$ (median $4.26$), $|\mathbf{v}_{\rm SW}| = 594.7\text{ km s}^{-1}$, $v_{\rm rel} = 551.5\text{ km s}^{-1}$, $\Phi_{p,\text{helio}} = 2.278\times 10^8\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$, **comet-frame incident flux $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 2.104\times 10^8\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$** (median $2.264\times 10^8\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$, $\Phi_{\rm hi,rel} = 1.353\times 10^5\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$).
     - **PN Frame Window (`Dec 3 12:04–Dec 4 10:12 UTC`)**: Mean $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 1.713\times 10^8$, **median $1.459\times 10^8\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$**.
     - **All-Pointing Window (`Dec 3 12:38–Dec 4 17:22 UTC`)**: Mean $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 1.376\times 10^8$, **median $9.425\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$**.

## 3. Convergence & Physical Sensitivity Highlights
- **Spatial Grid Convergence**: Relative to Fine `224x48x240` ($1.5^\circ$), Medium `120x24x120` ($3.0^\circ$) differs by **`-0.60%`** and Baseline `160x32x180` ($2.0^\circ$) differs by **`+2.14%`** in PN-GTI mean incident flux.
- **Temporal Step Size (CFL)**: Halving CFL (`0.175` vs. `0.35`) changes PN-GTI mean incident flux by **`+0.30%`**.
- **Latitude Domain Extent**: $\pm 30^\circ$ and $\pm 45^\circ$ domains differ from $\pm 60^\circ$ by **`-1.02%`** and **`+2.77%`**.
- **16 DONKI Cone CMEs (Including Nov 23 CMEs)**: `< 0.01%` difference during the Dec 3–4 window under measured launch speeds (`397` and `425 km/s`), as those fronts pass $1.87\text{ AU}$ on Nov 30–Dec 1.
- **Why 3D MHD ($\mathbf{B}\ne 0$) Is Crucial**: Our pure hydrodynamic control (`phys_hydro_only`, $\mathbf{B}=0$) over-compresses the CIR interface at $1.87\text{ AU}$ by **`+74.8%`** relative to full 3D MHD (`37.57e7` vs. `21.49e7 cm^-2 s^-1`), proving that fast-magnetosonic magnetic pressure support is essential when modeling stream interactions at $1.87\text{ AU}$.

### 1. Key Scientific Findings & Resolution of the Preprint vs. CCMC Discrepancy

1. **Why Uncalibrated CCMC ENLIL Predicts Lower Flux Than Ballistic 1 AU Extrapolations**:
   - Direct validation against native 1 AU in-situ measurements (`STEREO-A`, `Wind`, `ACE`, `Solar Orbiter`) over `2025-11-26` to `2025-12-05` demonstrates that the default uncalibrated CCMC WSA 5.4 + ENLIL 2.8f inner boundary (`dfast = 125 cm^-3` at $21.5\,R_\odot$) **systematically underpredicts 1 AU solar wind proton flux by a factor of $\sim 2\times$** (median model-to-observed flux ratio `0.50` at `STEREO-A` and `0.56` at `Wind`).
   - When our 3D spherical ideal-MHD solver ([`src/heliomhd3d.cu`](file:///mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/argon/src/heliomhd3d.cu)) is driven with the same uncalibrated CCMC-scale WSA boundary (**Model 1**, `model1_ccmc`), it reproduces CCMC ENLIL at 3I/ATLAS ($n_p = 0.87\text{ cm}^{-3}$, $|\mathbf{v}_{\rm SW}| = 480.5\text{ km s}^{-1}$, comet-frame speed $v_{\rm rel} = 443.2\text{ km s}^{-1}$, heliocentric flux $\Phi_{p,\text{helio}} = 4.16\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$, comet-frame incident flux $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 3.83\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$, vs. CCMC's $\Phi_{p,\text{helio}} = 4.51\times 10^7$ and $\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 4.07\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$).
   - Once the WSA 5.4 inner boundary is calibrated to observed 1 AU momentum flux (**Model 2**, `model2_wsa_cal`), the ambient 3D MHD proton flux at 3I/ATLAS doubles to **$\Phi_{p,\text{rel}} = 8.09\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$** ($\Phi_{p,\text{helio}} = 8.83\times 10^7\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$), closely matching the preprint's ballistic `STEREO-A` (`7.51e7` median, `9.24e7` mean) and `Wind` (`6.95e7` median, `7.35e7` mean) extrapolations.

2. **Multi-Spacecraft Assimilated 3D MHD (**Model 3**) & Out-of-Sample Holdout Validation**:
   - Assimilating the in-situ `STEREO-A` ($\text{lat} = -5.36^\circ$, separated by only $1.10^\circ$ in latitude from 3I/ATLAS at $-6.46^\circ$), `Wind`/`ACE` ($\text{lat} = +0.51^\circ$), and `Solar Orbiter` ($\text{lat} = +9.44^\circ$) streams onto the $0.10\text{ AU}$ inner boundary while preserving WSA 5.4 latitudinal structure (**Model 3**, `model3_assimilated`) achieves a 1 AU median flux ratio of `1.044` at `STEREO-A` (speed $r = 0.811$, $\text{RMSE} = 65.7\text{ km s}^{-1}$) and `1.031` at `Wind`.
   - An **out-of-sample holdout simulation** (`model3_holdout_wind`, trained strictly on `STEREO-A` + `Solar Orbiter` with `Wind` and `ACE` completely withheld) predicts the out-of-sample `Wind` (Earth L1) solar wind with speed $\text{RMSE} = 67.3\text{ km s}^{-1}$ ($r = 0.728$) and median proton flux ratio **`1.032`**.
   - In **Model 3**, the fast corotating stream and Corotating Interaction Region (CIR) observed by `STEREO-A` on Nov 28–29 steepens into a forward-reverse compression wave between $1.0\text{ AU}$ and $1.873\text{ AU}$.   - **3D Spherical Parker / Weber-Davis Steady Wind** ($48\times 12\times 48$, $96\times 24\times 96$, $192\times 48\times 192$): Conserves radial mass flux $r^2 \rho v_r$ across $0.10\text{--}2.40\text{ AU}$ to $< 0.87\%$ (`0.869%` on $192^3$) and radial magnetic flux $r^2 B_r$ to $< 10^{-8}$ relative to exact 1D ODE integration.
  - **3D Tilted-Dipole ($30^\circ$) CIR Benchmark** ($64\times 16\times 64$, $128\times 32\times 128$, $192\times 48\times 192$): Reproduces Pizzo (1991) 3D forward-reverse shock pair steepening, density pileup, and magnetic compression at $r = 1.873\text{ AU}$.
- **Spatial, Temporal & Domain Convergence at 3I/ATLAS** ([`fig_convergence_study.png`](file:///mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/argon/outputs/figures/fig_convergence_study.png)):

  - **Temporal Step Size (CFL)**: Halving CFL (`0.175` vs. `0.35`, doubling RK2 steps from $6{,}353$ to $12{,}705$) changes GTI mean incident flux by **`+0.30%`**.
  - **Latitudinal Domain Extent**: $\pm 30^\circ$ and $\pm 45^\circ$ domains differ from $\pm 60^\circ$ by **`-1.02%`** and **`+2.77%`**.
  - **Physical Controls**: Injecting all 16 DONKI cone CMEs (`phys_with_cmes`, including the two Nov 23 CMEs launched toward 3I/ATLAS's quadrant at $397$ and $425\text{ km s}^{-1}$) changes the Dec 3–4 GTI mean flux by **`< 0.01%`** because those CMEs pass $1.87\text{ AU}$ on Nov 30–Dec 1. Adiabatic $\gamma = 5/3$ (`phys_gamma_53`) increases CIR compression by `+12.14%`; turning off solar gravity (`phys_no_grav`) shifts the CIR arrival earlier (`-34.52%`); and turning off the magnetic field ($\mathbf{B}=0$, `phys_hydro_only`) over-compresses the CIR shock interface by **`+74.78%`**, demonstrating why full 3D MHD ($\mathbf{B} \ne 0$) is essential.
